label: NOT IN
note: NULLs in the comparison set can make NOT IN unknown rather than true. Excluding missing values or using a suitable NOT EXISTS pattern can be necessary.

label: COUNT()
note: COUNT(*) counts rows; COUNT(column) counts non-NULL values. In pandas, size and count are different operations.

label: CROSS JOIN
note: MySQL has no native FULL OUTER JOIN. A pandas outer merge is not a MySQL syntax example.

label: CASE
example: CASE WHEN x>0 THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END

label: REPLACE
note: REPLACE INTO is a row-write statement, not the string REPLACE() function. The reference example is a syntax fragment, not a safe update recipe.

label: ALTER TABLE
example: ALTER TABLE users ADD age INT

label: First row per group
example: ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY id ORDER BY d)

label: Anti-join
example: LEFT JOIN ... WHERE b.id IS NULL

label: Top N per group
example: ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY g ORDER BY x DESC)
note: ROW_NUMBER picks rows. DENSE_RANK picks distinct ranks and can retain extra tied rows. Choose the rule the question asks for.

label: LENGTH()
note: MySQL LENGTH measures bytes, not characters. Use CHAR_LENGTH for a character count.

label: DATEDIFF()
note: DATEDIFF(d1,d2) is d1 minus d2 using date parts. TIMESTAMPDIFF(unit,d1,d2) uses d2 minus d1.

label: TIMESTAMPDIFF()
note: The result is the difference from the second argument to the third, in the requested unit. This reverses the operand order compared with DATEDIFF.

label: LAST_VALUE()
note: LAST_VALUE uses the current window frame. To read the final value of the whole partition, an explicit frame ending at UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING is often required.

label: ORDER BY
note: This row is the ORDER BY inside OVER. Final result ordering is a separate ORDER BY on the outer query.

label: Rows by label
note: Label slicing includes the stop label when present. Positional iloc slicing excludes the stop position.

label: New column
note: Assign through the DataFrame itself. Chained assignment such as df["x"][mask] = value does not update the parent under Copy-on-Write.

label: np.where()
note: This is a NumPy function, used alongside pandas. It returns an array rather than a labeled Series.

label: First row per group
note: The image labels this “first row”, but groupby.first() takes the first non-missing value in each column by default. With missing data, those values can come from different rows. Sort and use groupby.head(1) when you need an intact row.

label: Last row per group
note: By default, groupby.last() skips missing values per column, so the result need not be one intact source row. Sort and use groupby.tail(1) for the last complete row selection.

label: First/last score
note: first and last aggregation skip missing values by default. Define tie-breaking and missing-score behavior when comparing dated endpoints.

label: query()
note: query and eval accept expressions, not arbitrary SQL. Do not construct them from untrusted user input.

label: Inner merge
note: Missing keys can match other missing keys in pandas. Use validate when the expected join cardinality matters.

label: Outer merge
note: pandas can match null merge keys to each other, unlike ordinary SQL equality joins. Also check whether the keys cause one-to-many or many-to-many matches.

label: sum()
note: Use min_count=1 when an all-missing input should stay missing instead of becoming zero, as discussed in the saved SQL/pandas comparison.

label: Basic group
note: pandas drops missing grouping keys by default; use dropna=False when those rows must form a group.

label: Percent change
note: Despite its name, pct_change returns fractional change. Multiply by 100 to express a percentage; handle missing values explicitly.

label: Contains
note: str.contains treats the pattern as a regular expression by default. Set regex=False for a literal substring and choose na behavior explicitly.

label: Rank
note: pandas rank() defaults to average ranks for ties. SQL RANK uses the minimum tied rank; rank(method="min") is the closer counterpart.

label: Percentile rank
note: pct=True scales pandas ranks; it is not generally the same formula as SQL PERCENT_RANK(). Non-missing percentile ranks lie in (0, 1].

label: LIMIT / OFFSET
description: Select a page of sorted results

label: NTH_VALUE()
example: NTH_VALUE(score, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY student_id ORDER BY exam_date)
description: Read the nth value in a window frame

label: EXTRACT()
description: Extract a date or time field

label: round()
note: Halfway rounding can differ from MySQL exact-value rounding; the setup page includes a half-up helper.

label: to_frame()
description: Convert a Series to a DataFrame

label: str.match()
description: Match from the start of a string
